passages: Jason Reding Quiñones led investigation into whether Trump’s rights were violated during 2020 election inquiry
Jason Reding Quiñones led investigation into whether Trump’s rights were violated during 2020 election inquiry

A US attorney overseeing the so-called “grand conspiracy” investigation into Donald Trump ’s rivals announced on Friday he is leaving the Department of Justice, one of several officials to leave the department in recent days after sweeping Democratic wins in the midterm elections .

Jason Reding Quiñones, the US attorney for the southern district of Florida, and John Eisenberg, who led the justice department’s national security division, are both leaving. Democrats have pledged to use their majorities in the US House and Senate to conduct aggressive oversight of the justice department, among other agencies.

Quiñones had been overseeing an inquiry into whether former top government officials engaged in a “grand conspiracy” to violate Trump’s rights when they investigated him after the 2020 election. Conservative allies had high hopes for the investigation, whose targets included the former CIA director John Brennan, among others.

But there were personnel issues and charges have not yet been filed. “The ‘grand conspiracy’ case into the lawfare against the president is essentially dead now,” Julie Kelly, a conservative commentator, posted on X .

“We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a statement.

Eisenberg led the national security division, which oversees terrorism and espionage cases, among others. Eisenberg had previously served in the first Trump administration and has been a top lawyer for the national security council. “He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic,” Blanche said in a post on X.

Harmeet Dhillon, the controversial head of the justice department’s civil rights division, also announced she was leaving on Thursday. Dhillon had sought to leave before the midterms and was asked by the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, to stay on until after election day.

CBS News reported on Thursday that Trump sought to dismiss Dhillon after her October appearance on 60 Minutes for not more forcefully defending efforts to prosecute non-citizens and send monitors to the polls.

Dhillon told the Guardian she submitted her resignation letter on 13 October, before the 60 Minutes interview aired, and that Wiles asked her to stay on until at least early November. She had also indicated to reporters in August she intended to return to private practice when she left the justice department, according to Bloomberg.

sources.title: 2 Justice Department officials resign, including U.S. attorney who oversaw 'grand conspiracy' probe
passages: Quiñones was confirmed by the Senate last year as U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, where the Justice Department had centered its meandering probe into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against the Republican president.

The top federal prosecutor in Miami who had been tasked with overseeing an investigation into foes of President Trump has resigned, joining other high-profile Justice Department officials departing in the wake of the midterm elections, officials said Friday.

Jason Reding Quiñones' resignation follows frustrations among Washington officials with his management of the office assigned to lead the so-called grand conspiracy investigation, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss personnel issues.

Eisenberg was sworn in as assistant attorney general in charge of the department’s National Security Division in June 2025 and oversaw cases involving espionage, terrorism, export control violations, cyber crimes and other matters.

Blanche said in a social media post that the department is grateful for Quiñones' "leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking, and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro." Castro, the former Cuban president, was indicted by Quiñones' office in May on charges related to the 1996 downing of civilian planes flown by Miami-based exiles.

Among the division’s most high-profile cases under his watch was the prosecution of former national security adviser John Bolton, who pleaded guilty this year to allegations of mishandling classified information and is awaiting sentencing.

Quiñones was confirmed by the Senate last year as U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, where the Justice Department had centered its meandering probe into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against the Republican president. His departure comes as the investigation has shown signs of faltering amid a spate of staff turnovers and delays. Investigators in recent weeks have put off scheduled grand jury testimony of several witnesses, according to multiple people familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing investigation. Quiñones said Friday that he is leaving with “immense pride in what we accomplished together and profound gratitude for the opportunity to serve our great Nation.” “I am grateful to President Trump for his trust and to the extraordinary men and women of the great Southern District of Florida for their dedication, friendship, and unwavering commitment to justice and the rule of law,” Quiñones wrote in a social media post. The “grand conspiracy" investigation has proceeded in fits and starts for over a year with repeated setbacks and departures. Last April, a lead national security prosecutor in the investigation of former CIA Director John Brennan was replaced on the team after raising questions about the strength of the case. Shortly afterward, Joseph diGenova, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, took over the probe. DiGenova resigned from the Justice Department in September without bringing any criminal charges. extraction.body: John Eisenberg, the head of the National Security Division at the Department of Justice, is stepping down from his post, becoming the third senior DOJ official to resign since the midterm elections. Shortly after Fox News learned of Eisenberg's resignation, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced it on social media. "He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic," Blanche said. "Under his leadership, the Division advanced President Trump’s mission to make America safe by prosecuting terrorists and working with our law enforcement partners to disrupt planned attacks on the American people." This was Eisenberg's second stint serving under President Donald Trump. In Trump's first term, Eisenberg was an assistant and deputy counsel to the president, as well as a legal advisor to the National Security Council, which advises presidents on foreign policy matters. DOJ CIVIL RIGHTS CHIEF HARMEET DHILLON RESIGNS, SAYS WHITE HOUSE ASKED HER TO WAIT UNTIL AFTER MIDTERMS Less than an hour before Eisenberg's departure was made public, Blanche announced the resignation of Jason Reding Quiñones, the U.S. Quiñones was perhaps best known for securing an indictment against Raúl Castro, the former president of Cuba who took over after his brother Fidel Castro's nearly 50-year reign. Raúl Castro, now 95, was indicted for his alleged role in the 1996 shoot-down of two unarmed civilian aircraft operated by Brothers to the Rescue, a Miami-based humanitarian group that searched the Florida Straits for Cuban migrants in distress. "We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combatting violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking, and transnational crime," Blanche said. "Jason has served the Department multiple times over his distinguished career, and we thank him for his service to this country." DOJ LAUNCHES CRIMINAL PROBE INTO SUPREME COURT LEAK THAT EXPOSED RULING OVERTURNING ROE V WADE The departure of Eisenberg and Quiñones came just a day after Harmeet Dhillon, who headed up the DOJ's Civil Rights Division, announced she'd be leaving as well. In an interview with Fox News Digital, Dhillon said she attempted to resign three weeks ago but was asked by White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles to stay until after the midterms. Dhillon moved to Washington following the deaths of her husband and father to "serve my country," but after roughly two years in the administration, she said it was time for her to leave. In the lead-up to the midterms, Dhillon defended the Trump administration's investigation into noncitizen voters. She was also in charge of the DOJ's effort to send more than 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states.

Jason Reding Quiñones, the US attorney for the southern district of Florida, and John Eisenberg, who led the justice department’s national security division, are both leaving. Democrats have pledged to use their majorities in the US House and Senate to conduct aggressive oversight of the justice department, among other agencies. Quiñones had been overseeing an inquiry into whether former top government officials engaged in a “grand conspiracy” to violate Trump’s rights when they investigated him after the 2020 election. Conservative allies had high hopes for the investigation, whose targets included the former CIA director John Brennan, among others. But there were personnel issues and charges have not yet been filed. “The ‘grand conspiracy’ case into the lawfare against the president is essentially dead now,” Julie Kelly, a conservative commentator, posted on X . “We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a statement. Eisenberg led the national security division, which oversees terrorism and espionage cases, among others. Eisenberg had previously served in the first Trump administration and has been a top lawyer for the national security council. “He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic,” Blanche said in a post on X. Harmeet Dhillon, the controversial head of the justice department’s civil rights division, also announced she was leaving on Thursday. Dhillon had sought to leave before the midterms and was asked by the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, to stay on until after election day. CBS News reported on Thursday that Trump sought to dismiss Dhillon after her October appearance on 60 Minutes for not more forcefully defending efforts to prosecute non-citizens and send monitors to the polls. Dhillon told the Guardian she submitted her resignation letter on 13 October, before the 60 Minutes interview aired, and that Wiles asked her to stay on until at least early November. She had also indicated to reporters in August she intended to return to private practice when she left the justice department, according to Bloomberg.

Jason Reding Quiñones led investigation into whether Trump’s rights were violated during 2020 election inquiry

A US attorney overseeing the so-called “grand conspiracy” investigation into Donald Trump ’s rivals announced on Friday he is leaving the Department of Justice, one of several officials to leave the department in recent days after sweeping Democratic wins in the midterm elections .

Jason Reding Quiñones, the US attorney for the southern district of Florida, and John Eisenberg, who led the justice department’s national security division, are both leaving. Democrats have pledged to use their majorities in the US House and Senate to conduct aggressive oversight of the justice department, among other agencies.

Quiñones had been overseeing an inquiry into whether former top government officials engaged in a “grand conspiracy” to violate Trump’s rights when they investigated him after the 2020 election. Conservative allies had high hopes for the investigation, whose targets included the former CIA director John Brennan, among others.

But there were personnel issues and charges have not yet been filed. “The ‘grand conspiracy’ case into the lawfare against the president is essentially dead now,” Julie Kelly, a conservative commentator, posted on X .

“We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a statement.

Eisenberg led the national security division, which oversees terrorism and espionage cases, among others. Eisenberg had previously served in the first Trump administration and has been a top lawyer for the national security council. “He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic,” Blanche said in a post on X.

Harmeet Dhillon, the controversial head of the justice department’s civil rights division, also announced she was leaving on Thursday. Dhillon had sought to leave before the midterms and was asked by the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, to stay on until after election day.

CBS News reported on Thursday that Trump sought to dismiss Dhillon after her October appearance on 60 Minutes for not more forcefully defending efforts to prosecute non-citizens and send monitors to the polls.

Dhillon told the Guardian she submitted her resignation letter on 13 October, before the 60 Minutes interview aired, and that Wiles asked her to stay on until at least early November. She had also indicated to reporters in August she intended to return to private practice when she left the justice department, according to Bloomberg.

extraction.body: John Eisenberg, the head of the National Security Division at the Department of Justice, is stepping down from his post, becoming the third senior DOJ official to resign since the midterm elections. Shortly after Fox News learned of Eisenberg's resignation, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced it on social media. "He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic," Blanche said. "Under his leadership, the Division advanced President Trump’s mission to make America safe by prosecuting terrorists and working with our law enforcement partners to disrupt planned attacks on the American people." This was Eisenberg's second stint serving under President Donald Trump. In Trump's first term, Eisenberg was an assistant and deputy counsel to the president, as well as a legal advisor to the National Security Council, which advises presidents on foreign policy matters. DOJ CIVIL RIGHTS CHIEF HARMEET DHILLON RESIGNS, SAYS WHITE HOUSE ASKED HER TO WAIT UNTIL AFTER MIDTERMS Less than an hour before Eisenberg's departure was made public, Blanche announced the resignation of Jason Reding Quiñones, the U.S. Quiñones was perhaps best known for securing an indictment against Raúl Castro, the former president of Cuba who took over after his brother Fidel Castro's nearly 50-year reign. Raúl Castro, now 95, was indicted for his alleged role in the 1996 shoot-down of two unarmed civilian aircraft operated by Brothers to the Rescue, a Miami-based humanitarian group that searched the Florida Straits for Cuban migrants in distress. "We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combatting violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking, and transnational crime," Blanche said. "Jason has served the Department multiple times over his distinguished career, and we thank him for his service to this country." DOJ LAUNCHES CRIMINAL PROBE INTO SUPREME COURT LEAK THAT EXPOSED RULING OVERTURNING ROE V WADE The departure of Eisenberg and Quiñones came just a day after Harmeet Dhillon, who headed up the DOJ's Civil Rights Division, announced she'd be leaving as well. In an interview with Fox News Digital, Dhillon said she attempted to resign three weeks ago but was asked by White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles to stay until after the midterms. Dhillon moved to Washington following the deaths of her husband and father to "serve my country," but after roughly two years in the administration, she said it was time for her to leave. In the lead-up to the midterms, Dhillon defended the Trump administration's investigation into noncitizen voters. She was also in charge of the DOJ's effort to send more than 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states.

sources.title: The iPhone Duo has more than 100,000 optimized apps, Apple says
passages: Apple’s iPhone Duo has been officially on sale for two weeks, and the company said today that the App Store now has over 100,000 apps that are built for the foldable.

extraction.body: Apple’s iPhone Duo has been officially on sale for two weeks, and the company said today that the App Store now has over 100,000 apps that are built for the foldable. “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” Susan Prescott, Apple’s VP of Worldwide Developer Relations, says in a statement. “Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day.” Prescott adds that “the enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.” Although there are now many apps that are optimized for the Duo, they can sometimes still have some issues. When the Duo launched, users noted that the Instagram app was a little messy even though Apple gave it the “Made for iPhone Duo” label, and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri called the Duo a “bit of a tricky form factor.”

Recent apps optimized for iPhone Duo include Microsoft Word , Microsoft Outlook , Zoom , Etsy , Halide Mark III , and more. I detailed the iPhone Duo app experience in my full review last month . At the time, I emphasized the big difference between using an app updated for iPhone Duo and one that isn’t. I’m thrilled to see how quickly the apps I use every day are being updated for iPhone Duo. Another trend I’m noticing is that apps that were quick to support iPhone Duo at launch have since received subsequent updates with better optimization for the inner and outer displays. sources.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple
passages: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch.
But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front.

The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year.
On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve .
The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added.
Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo.
However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon.

extraction.body: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu. Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve . “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note. Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple’s iPhone Duo has been officially on sale for two weeks, and the company said today that the App Store now has over 100,000 apps that are built for the foldable.
Apple released the iPhone Duo two weeks ago, and the app story is quickly taking shape.
“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation.
In total, Apple says that over 2,000 developers have attended more than 50 in-person workshops around the world.
Recent apps optimized for iPhone Duo include Microsoft Word , Microsoft Outlook , Zoom , Etsy , Halide Mark III , and more.
Another trend I’m noticing is that apps that were quick to support iPhone Duo at launch have since received subsequent updates with better optimization for the inner and outer displays.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:
Here’s Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations:
The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch.
But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front.

The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year.
On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve .
The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added.
Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo.
However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon.

sources.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple
passages: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch.
But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front.

The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year.
On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve .
The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added.
Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo.
However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon.

extraction.body: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later , meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays and have vertical controls in the status bar. A statement from Susan Prescott, Apple's Vice President of Worldwide Developer Relations: It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day. In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we're excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo. Apple said thousands of apps optimized for the iPhone Duo are being added to the App Store each day, with recent examples including Microsoft's Excel, OneNote, PowerPoint, and Word apps , along with the Etsy, Goodnotes, Halide Mark III, NBA, NHL, and Zoom apps. Other apps optimized for the device include Amazon Prime Video, Fantastical, Flighty, Instagram, MLB, Netflix, SmartGym, WhatsApp, YouTube, and more. There are too many to list. Apps optimized for the iPhone Duo have a "Made for iPhone Duo" badge in their App Store listings on the device, making them easy to identify. iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support to the iPhone Duo , enabling users to draw in apps like Procreate Pocket, take notes in Apple Notes, Fineliner, and TypeDraw, and mark up documents in apps like Preview on the device. On the other hand, with millions of apps available in the App Store, there are unsurprisingly many apps that are still not optimized for the iPhone Duo, with the following examples listed in alphabetical order: AMC Theaters, Amazon Fire TV, Apple Store, Best Buy, Bluesky, Delta, DoorDash, Duolingo, Fandango, FedEx, Goodreads, Google Docs, Google Home, Google Sheets, Google Slides, GrubHub, JetBlue, Libby, Microsoft Authenticator, Microsoft Teams, MTA, Nike, PayPal, PictureThis, Ring, Southwest, Spectrum TV, Starbucks, Steam, Uber Eats, UPS, USPS, Venmo, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Whole Foods, and YouTube Music. Apple said developers can easily optimize their apps for the iPhone Duo. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, with controls moved to the status bar and multi-column support on the inner display. New APIs let developers optimize their apps for the device's various layouts and poses. Apple has hosted more than 50 in-person iPhone Duo app workshops in 19 cities worldwide, and there are online resources like the Apple Developer Forums . In the meantime, apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of the inner display on the iPhone Duo, but they avoid the status bar on the right edge. Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier run on the iPhone Duo, but appear in the center of the inner display, with lots of empty black space on the left and right sides of the apps. iPhone Duo app optimization has been a hotly debated topic on social media platforms, with some people pointing out apps that are not yet optimized and others saying the issue is overblown. It is clearly a mixed bag, with some apps optimized and some not. More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly. sources.title: The New York Times Company Is Reportedly Trying To Buy Letterboxd For $330 Million - Engadget
passages: The company that owns The New York Times is in "exclusive negotiations" to purchase the cinephile online platform Letterboxd, anonymous sources told...
The price being discussed is reportedly around $330 million, significantly more than the $250 million figure that was bandied around earlier this year .
Discussions are ongoing and could still break down, the report states.
Letterboxd would reportedly continue operations as a standalone site for the "foreseeable future," the NYT reported.
The Times Company also has a similar business model with a mix of ad and subscription revenue.
Though relatively small with 30 million members, Letterboxd is an influential online film site with a dedicated and active community that includes notable figures like Martin Scorsese .

extraction.body: Letterboxd would reportedly continue operations as a standalone site. The company that owns The New York Times is in "exclusive negotiations" to purchase the cinephile online platform Letterboxd, anonymous sources told... The New York Times . The price being discussed is reportedly around $330 million, significantly more than the $250 million figure that was bandied around earlier this year . Discussions are ongoing and could still break down, the report states. Letterboxd would reportedly continue operations as a standalone site for the "foreseeable future," the NYT reported. However, the Times Company could introduce its own advertising technology into Letterboxd's systems. (The New York Times Company declined to confirm the New York Times' reporting.) With its "social film discovery" tagline, Letterboxd allows members to create curated lists, diaries, logs, ratings and reviews of movies, while following other members' activities — a Goodreads for movies, if you will. Though relatively small with 30 million members, Letterboxd is an influential online film site with a dedicated and active community that includes notable figures like Martin Scorsese . The site is projected to have $15 million in revenue for 2026. The Canadian investment group Tiny purchased 60 percent of Letterboxd in 2023, but reportedly started seeking a sale in July this year at a valuation of around $250 million. The list of potential suitors at the time was a who's who of Hollywood, with Netflix, Paramount and Sony Pictures all reportedly interested. The New York Times Company is now in the mix at a higher price, and is arguably a better buyer because it wouldn't pose a conflict of interest like those Hollywood studios. The Times Company also has a similar business model with a mix of ad and subscription revenue. The NYT website currently has 13.8 million subscribers, with a goal to hit 15 million by the end of next year. Much of the site's traffic is driven by its puzzle games like Wordle, along with recipes and its sports site, The Athletic . Letterboxd could fit neatly into that mix, offering readers a new way to discover and explore films.

The price being discussed is reportedly around $330 million, significantly more than the $250 million figure that was bandied around earlier this year . Discussions are ongoing and could still break down, the report states. Letterboxd would reportedly continue operations as a standalone site for the "foreseeable future," the NYT reported. However, the Times Company could introduce its own advertising technology into Letterboxd's systems. (The New York Times Company declined to confirm the New York Times' reporting.) With its "social film discovery" tagline, Letterboxd allows members to create curated lists, diaries, logs, ratings and reviews of movies, while following other members' activities — a Goodreads for movies, if you will. Though relatively small with 30 million members, Letterboxd is an influential online film site with a dedicated and active community that includes notable figures like Martin Scorsese . The site is projected to have $15 million in revenue for 2026. The Canadian investment group Tiny purchased 60 percent of Letterboxd in 2023, but reportedly started seeking a sale in July this year at a valuation of around $250 million. The list of potential suitors at the time was a who's who of Hollywood, with Netflix, Paramount and Sony Pictures all reportedly interested. The New York Times Company is now in the mix at a higher price, and is arguably a better buyer because it wouldn't pose a conflict of interest like those Hollywood studios. The Times Company also has a similar business model with a mix of ad and subscription revenue. The NYT website currently has 13.8 million subscribers, with a goal to hit 15 million by the end of next year. Much of the site's traffic is driven by its puzzle games like Wordle, along with recipes and its sports site, The Athletic . Letterboxd could fit neatly into that mix, offering readers a new way to discover and explore films.

The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public sources have revealed a long list of high-profile customers, including government agencies such as the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, and the US Air Force, as well as private companies such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It’s unclear if the data theft exposed customers to additional threats. Last Friday, Chainalysis said it had been the target of a cybersecurity incident in October that was similar to the hacks of other platforms during the same month. The external actor used AI agent-assisted offensive techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools. An email the company sent to affected customers said some “non-sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed.” It’s not clear why the company considered such information “non-sensitive.” In a Wednesday update, the company said that part of the “ongoing multifront cyberattack” involved an “on-path attack” that exposed a subset of customer passwords, and that the attack vector had been identified and fixed. Also known as an adversary-in-the-middle attack, on-path attacks happen when a hacker gains access to a piece of infrastructure sending traffic back and forth between two parties. Chainalysis has yet to say where the infrastructure compromise occurred and if the data obtained from it was TLS encrypted. The company said later that day that an investigation two days earlier (on Monday) had revealed that “certain customer information including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed to a malicious actor.” It also said it had detected “abnormal activity” and, in response, took down its login page and know-your-transaction service, which monitors threats to cryptocurrency holdings in real time. The company has also removed access to its Reactor and Data Solutions services. It asked customers to submit their trusted IP addresses so they can be added to an allow list and to prepare to reset credentials once they regain access. The credential rotation is mandatory. The company says its investigation has yet to reveal any evidence that any investigation data has been accessed or Chainalysis attribution data has been manipulated. It’s not clear how useful the information obtained in such an attack would be unless the attackers also had the ability to decrypt the traffic they were monitoring. sources.title: Chainalysis confirms user credentials exposed in cyberattack, takes services offline
passages: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis has confirmed that hackers exposed password hashes and live tokens belonging to its users during a cyberattack that forced several of its investigation and transaction monitoring services offline.

In an email sent to certain affected users, Chainalysis described the incident as an "ongoing multifront cyberattack" and confirmed that an "on-path attack" had exposed a subset of customer passwords.

The latest disclosure expands on an October 30 statement in which Chainalysis initially reported that certain customer profile details had been accessed but said it had found no evidence of compromised authentication credentials or session tokens.
Following the November 2 Mercado Bitcoin attack, Chainalysis said it helped coordinate the freezing of nearly $10 million in stolen cryptocurrency.
Two days later, abnormal activity prompted Chainalysis to suspend KYT's user interface and API, other address screening products and its login page.

In its instructions to affected customers, Chainalysis warned users against following links in unsolicited password reset emails and advised anyone who reused their Chainalysis password elsewhere to change those credentials.
Customers will be required to reset passwords and rotate API keys where appropriate, while Chainalysis works to restore access through approved IP addresses.
Chainalysis explicitly stated that its own security incident was unrelated to the Binance theft.
Its initial investigation identified exposed user IDs, email addresses, full names and organizational roles, while the company worked to determine which customer records had been affected.

Chainalysis confirmed that customer names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens belonging to all users were exposed to a malicious actor during a cyberattack. The company took KYT, Reactor, Data Solutions and other screening products offline after detecting suspicious activity, with some customer accounts potentially accessed without authorization. Chainalysis identified an on path attack that exposed a subset of customer passwords and said the attack method had since been contained and remediated. According to a November 4 security update, the company discovered that customer information, including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users, had been exposed to a malicious actor. The company has since identified suspicious activity involving its Know Your Transaction (KYT) service and is contacting customers whose accounts appear to have been accessed without authorization. Chainalysis said it continues to have no evidence that investigation data was accessed or that its blockchain attribution data was manipulated during the incident. Chainalysis cyberattack exposes passwords and live tokens The security incident was first disclosed on October 30 after Chainalysis detected an external attacker using what it described as "offensive agentic techniques" to gain unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools. Its initial investigation identified exposed user IDs, email addresses, full names and organizational roles, while the company worked to determine which customer records had been affected. In an email sent to certain affected users, Chainalysis described the incident as an "ongoing multifront cyberattack" and confirmed that an "on-path attack" had exposed a subset of customer passwords. An on-path attack allows an intruder to intercept communications between a user and a service. Chainalysis said it had contained and remediated the attack method and was locking affected accounts as a precaution. The exposure of password hashes and live tokens presents separate security concerns. Password hashes are stored representations of passwords, while active authentication tokens can potentially provide access to services without requiring users to enter their passwords again. Chainalysis has not disclosed the hashing method used to protect passwords or specified the type of live tokens involved. The company has brought in third-party cybersecurity specialists to investigate the intrusion and strengthen its systems, with large language models being used to support its internal security review. Chainalysis suspends KYT and Reactor services after suspicious activity The breach has forced Chainalysis to suspend several products used by cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions and law enforcement agencies. On November 2, the company took Reactor and Data Solutions offline for additional security assessments while allowing its compliance transaction monitoring products to continue operating. Reactor provides blockchain investigation tools, while Data Solutions supplies blockchain data used by customers for analysis and monitoring. Two days later, abnormal activity prompted Chainalysis to suspend KYT's user interface and API, other address screening products and its login page. Its API allows customers to connect transaction screening directly to their existing systems. Chainalysis said it intended to begin restoring KYT and Address Screening access on November 5, initially through an allowlist of trusted customer IP addresses. Customers were instructed to contact their account teams or support staff with approved IP addresses before receiving access to reset passwords and rotate API keys. Every user will be required to reset their password, with API key rotation required where appropriate. The company has not provided a restoration date for Reactor or Data Solutions. Recent crypto attacks put security controls under scrutiny The incident follows several major cybersecurity breaches affecting cryptocurrency companies in recent weeks. As crypto.news previously reported, Binance suffered an estimated $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft on October 29 after attackers compromised systems connected to its wallet infrastructure. Chainalysis explicitly stated that its own security incident was unrelated to the Binance theft. The blockchain analytics company has continued assisting other firms with security investigations during the disruption. Following the November 2 Mercado Bitcoin attack, Chainalysis said it helped coordinate the freezing of nearly $10 million in stolen cryptocurrency. Separately, Binance revoked API keys associated with trading platform SignalPlus on November 5 after the third-party service reported a security incident. SignalPlus subsequently acknowledged that some affected accounts lacked mandatory IP whitelisting, while Binance and Deribit disabled connected credentials as a precaution. In its instructions to affected customers, Chainalysis warned users against following links in unsolicited password reset emails and advised anyone who reused their Chainalysis password elsewhere to change those credentials. The company recommended two-factor authentication for organizations that had not enabled it and asked customers to report suspicious communications or account activity to their security teams.

extraction.body: Smarter Insights for a Fast-Moving Digital World DreamHost told California’s attorney general that hackers obtained customer session tokens and login credentials in an attack that began in August 2026. The web host didn’t catch the intrusion, which ran through third-party software behind its File Manager, until October 23. As first reported by TechCrunch , the breach notice says the attackers took session tokens. Those tokens keep a user signed in after entering a password, so whoever holds one can act as that user. DreamHost’s own incident notice explains where the credentials came from. The attacker could see the FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords of anyone who logged into File Manager before the intrusion was caught. It also obtained webmail logins for a limited number of users and, in a small number of cases, may have viewed mailbox contents. The breach first surfaced as a File Manager outage and a round of forced email and FTP password resets . DreamHost first called those resets a precaution. Its advice now is blunter: “ Please treat those usernames and passwords as compromised. “ File Manager’s design made it an efficient target. Customers typed FTP credentials into one web front end, so a single compromised server could collect logins from every user who passed through it. DreamHost reset affected passwords and ended active sessions on the day it found the intrusion. The second step matters as much as the first, because a stolen token can outlive a password change. 🚨🇺🇸 DreamHost Confirms Data Breach, Hackers Stole Customer Credentials and Accessed Email Inboxes Web hosting provider DreamHost has confirmed that hackers gained unauthorized access to its systems during a months-long cyberattack, stealing customer credentials and potentially accessing private email communications. The intrusion began in August 2026 and remained undetected until October 23, when DreamHost discovered attackers had exploited a vulnerability in its web-based File Manager. The attackers obtained FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords, along with webmail credentials and session tokens. In some cases, the stolen credentials may have allowed hackers to access customer inboxes and read private emails. DreamHost | Security Incident • Attack period: August to October 23, 2026 • Affected accounts: Well under 10% • Exposed: FTP/SFTP credentials and webmail login information • Impact: Potential unauthorized access to customer email accounts • Vulnerability: Undisclosed File Manager security flaw • Investigation: Ongoing DreamHost says it has blocked the attackers, patched the vulnerability, and reset affected credentials. The company found no evidence that customer billing information or control panel credentials were compromised. The exact number of affected customers remains undisclosed. A DreamHost spokesperson declined to explain why detection took so long, citing the ongoing investigation. The company hasn’t named the vulnerable software, published a CVE identifier or described the flaw. It did say the incident has no connection to recent PHP server updates, which it patched within hours of their release. The damage estimate has shifted, too. DreamHost says its precautionary notices reached more customers than investigators now believe were affected, so a reset email doesn’t confirm exposure. It doesn’t store full payment card numbers either, since a third party processes payments. Those no-evidence findings reflect the investigation so far, and the forensic work continues. Only the DreamHost account holder can assign new passwords through the control panel, and changes take up to 15 minutes. These steps help reduce risk for anyone who used File Manager or webmail during the window: Customers should also expect copycat messages, since breach notices make convenient phishing email bait. DreamHost says its incident emails never ask for passwords or send sign-in links, so users should type panel.dreamhost.com into the browser directly. DreamHost says it rebuilt File Manager with extra monitoring and rotated internal credentials that may have been exposed. It’s also reviewing other customer-facing tools for similar weaknesses. The next step is formal breach notices to customers and regulators, which the company is still preparing. Those letters may be the first place DreamHost commits to a firm count of how many accounts the attacker actually reached. This article has been reviewed and fact-checked by Robert A. Lee. extraction.body: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis has confirmed that hackers exposed password hashes and live tokens belonging to its users during a cyberattack that forced several of its investigation and transaction monitoring services offline. Chainalysis confirmed that customer names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens belonging to all users were exposed to a malicious actor during a cyberattack. The company took KYT, Reactor, Data Solutions and other screening products offline after detecting suspicious activity, with some customer accounts potentially accessed without authorization. Chainalysis identified an on path attack that exposed a subset of customer passwords and said the attack method had since been contained and remediated. Customers will be required to reset passwords and rotate API keys where appropriate, while Chainalysis works to restore access through approved IP addresses. According to a November 4 security update, the company discovered that customer information, including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users, had been exposed to a malicious actor. The latest disclosure expands on an October 30 statement in which Chainalysis initially reported that certain customer profile details had been accessed but said it had found no evidence of compromised authentication credentials or session tokens. The company has since identified suspicious activity involving its Know Your Transaction (KYT) service and is contacting customers whose accounts appear to have been accessed without authorization. Chainalysis said it continues to have no evidence that investigation data was accessed or that its blockchain attribution data was manipulated during the incident. Chainalysis cyberattack exposes passwords and live tokens The security incident was first disclosed on October 30 after Chainalysis detected an external attacker using what it described as "offensive agentic techniques" to gain unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools. Its initial investigation identified exposed user IDs, email addresses, full names and organizational roles, while the company worked to determine which customer records had been affected. In an email sent to certain affected users, Chainalysis described the incident as an "ongoing multifront cyberattack" and confirmed that an "on-path attack" had exposed a subset of customer passwords. An on-path attack allows an intruder to intercept communications between a user and a service. Chainalysis said it had contained and remediated the attack method and was locking affected accounts as a precaution. The exposure of password hashes and live tokens presents separate security concerns. Password hashes are stored representations of passwords, while active authentication tokens can potentially provide access to services without requiring users to enter their passwords again. Chainalysis has not disclosed the hashing method used to protect passwords or specified the type of live tokens involved. The company has brought in third-party cybersecurity specialists to investigate the intrusion and strengthen its systems, with large language models being used to support its internal security review. Chainalysis suspends KYT and Reactor services after suspicious activity The breach has forced Chainalysis to suspend several products used by cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions and law enforcement agencies. On November 2, the company took Reactor and Data Solutions offline for additional security assessments while allowing its compliance transaction monitoring products to continue operating. Reactor provides blockchain investigation tools, while Data Solutions supplies blockchain data used by customers for analysis and monitoring. Two days later, abnormal activity prompted Chainalysis to suspend KYT's user interface and API, other address screening products and its login page. Its API allows customers to connect transaction screening directly to their existing systems. Chainalysis said it intended to begin restoring KYT and Address Screening access on November 5, initially through an allowlist of trusted customer IP addresses. Customers were instructed to contact their account teams or support staff with approved IP addresses before receiving access to reset passwords and rotate API keys. Every user will be required to reset their password, with API key rotation required where appropriate. The company has not provided a restoration date for Reactor or Data Solutions. Recent crypto attacks put security controls under scrutiny The incident follows several major cybersecurity breaches affecting cryptocurrency companies in recent weeks. As crypto.news previously reported, Binance suffered an estimated $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft on October 29 after attackers compromised systems connected to its wallet infrastructure. Chainalysis explicitly stated that its own security incident was unrelated to the Binance theft. The blockchain analytics company has continued assisting other firms with security investigations during the disruption. Following the November 2 Mercado Bitcoin attack, Chainalysis said it helped coordinate the freezing of nearly $10 million in stolen cryptocurrency. Separately, Binance revoked API keys associated with trading platform SignalPlus on November 5 after the third-party service reported a security incident. SignalPlus subsequently acknowledged that some affected accounts lacked mandatory IP whitelisting, while Binance and Deribit disabled connected credentials as a precaution. In its instructions to affected customers, Chainalysis warned users against following links in unsolicited password reset emails and advised anyone who reused their Chainalysis password elsewhere to change those credentials. The company recommended two-factor authentication for organizations that had not enabled it and asked customers to report suspicious communications or account activity to their security teams.

extraction.body: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later , meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays and have vertical controls in the status bar. A statement from Susan Prescott, Apple's Vice President of Worldwide Developer Relations: It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day. In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we're excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo. Apple said thousands of apps optimized for the iPhone Duo are being added to the App Store each day, with recent examples including Microsoft's Excel, OneNote, PowerPoint, and Word apps , along with the Etsy, Goodnotes, Halide Mark III, NBA, NHL, and Zoom apps. Other apps optimized for the device include Amazon Prime Video, Fantastical, Flighty, Instagram, MLB, Netflix, SmartGym, WhatsApp, YouTube, and more. There are too many to list. Apps optimized for the iPhone Duo have a "Made for iPhone Duo" badge in their App Store listings on the device, making them easy to identify. iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support to the iPhone Duo , enabling users to draw in apps like Procreate Pocket, take notes in Apple Notes, Fineliner, and TypeDraw, and mark up documents in apps like Preview on the device. On the other hand, with millions of apps available in the App Store, there are unsurprisingly many apps that are still not optimized for the iPhone Duo, with the following examples listed in alphabetical order: AMC Theaters, Amazon Fire TV, Apple Store, Best Buy, Bluesky, Delta, DoorDash, Duolingo, Fandango, FedEx, Goodreads, Google Docs, Google Home, Google Sheets, Google Slides, GrubHub, JetBlue, Libby, Microsoft Authenticator, Microsoft Teams, MTA, Nike, PayPal, PictureThis, Ring, Southwest, Spectrum TV, Starbucks, Steam, Uber Eats, UPS, USPS, Venmo, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Whole Foods, and YouTube Music. Apple said developers can easily optimize their apps for the iPhone Duo. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, with controls moved to the status bar and multi-column support on the inner display. New APIs let developers optimize their apps for the device's various layouts and poses. Apple has hosted more than 50 in-person iPhone Duo app workshops in 19 cities worldwide, and there are online resources like the Apple Developer Forums . In the meantime, apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of the inner display on the iPhone Duo, but they avoid the status bar on the right edge. Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier run on the iPhone Duo, but appear in the center of the inner display, with lots of empty black space on the left and right sides of the apps. iPhone Duo app optimization has been a hotly debated topic on social media platforms, with some people pointing out apps that are not yet optimized and others saying the issue is overblown. It is clearly a mixed bag, with some apps optimized and some not. More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly. In a new statement to 9to5Mac , Apple has revealed that there are already “well over 100,000 apps” on the App Store designed for iPhone Duo, and thousands are being added each day. Here’s Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations: “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.” In total, Apple says that over 2,000 developers have attended more than 50 in-person workshops around the world. Apple is continuing to spotlight apps for iPhone Duo on the App Store, including editorial curations like “Popular Apps on iPhone Duo” and “Great Games on iPhone Duo.” There’s also a “Made for iPhone Duo” badge that appears on product pages for apps optimized for Apple’s foldable. Recent apps optimized for iPhone Duo include Microsoft Word , Microsoft Outlook , Zoom , Etsy , Halide Mark III , and more. I detailed the iPhone Duo app experience in my full review last month . At the time, I emphasized the big difference between using an app updated for iPhone Duo and one that isn’t. I’m thrilled to see how quickly the apps I use every day are being updated for iPhone Duo. Another trend I’m noticing is that apps that were quick to support iPhone Duo at launch have since received subsequent updates with better optimization for the inner and outer displays. extraction.body: Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago. We confirmed that this figure refers to apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later , meaning these apps fill the full width of the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays and have vertical controls in the status bar. A statement from Susan Prescott, Apple's Vice President of Worldwide Developer Relations: It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation. Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day. In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users. The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we're excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo. Apple said thousands of apps optimized for the iPhone Duo are being added to the App Store each day, with recent examples including Microsoft's Excel, OneNote, PowerPoint, and Word apps , along with the Etsy, Goodnotes, Halide Mark III, NBA, NHL, and Zoom apps. Other apps optimized for the device include Amazon Prime Video, Fantastical, Flighty, Instagram, MLB, Netflix, SmartGym, WhatsApp, YouTube, and more. There are too many to list. Apps optimized for the iPhone Duo have a "Made for iPhone Duo" badge in their App Store listings on the device, making them easy to identify. iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support to the iPhone Duo , enabling users to draw in apps like Procreate Pocket, take notes in Apple Notes, Fineliner, and TypeDraw, and mark up documents in apps like Preview on the device. On the other hand, with millions of apps available in the App Store, there are unsurprisingly many apps that are still not optimized for the iPhone Duo, with the following examples listed in alphabetical order: AMC Theaters, Amazon Fire TV, Apple Store, Best Buy, Bluesky, Delta, DoorDash, Duolingo, Fandango, FedEx, Goodreads, Google Docs, Google Home, Google Sheets, Google Slides, GrubHub, JetBlue, Libby, Microsoft Authenticator, Microsoft Teams, MTA, Nike, PayPal, PictureThis, Ring, Southwest, Spectrum TV, Starbucks, Steam, Uber Eats, UPS, USPS, Venmo, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Whole Foods, and YouTube Music. Apple said developers can easily optimize their apps for the iPhone Duo. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, with controls moved to the status bar and multi-column support on the inner display. New APIs let developers optimize their apps for the device's various layouts and poses. Apple has hosted more than 50 in-person iPhone Duo app workshops in 19 cities worldwide, and there are online resources like the Apple Developer Forums . In the meantime, apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of the inner display on the iPhone Duo, but they avoid the status bar on the right edge. Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier run on the iPhone Duo, but appear in the center of the inner display, with lots of empty black space on the left and right sides of the apps. iPhone Duo app optimization has been a hotly debated topic on social media platforms, with some people pointing out apps that are not yet optimized and others saying the issue is overblown. It is clearly a mixed bag, with some apps optimized and some not. More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly. For iPhone Duo owners, the milestone means a growing selection of apps can make better use of the 7.6-inch inner display rather than simply appearing as enlarged versions of traditional iPhone apps. Optimized layouts can provide more room for content, navigation and multitasking when the phone is unfolded.

Apple highlights compatible software through App Store collections including “Popular Apps on iPhone Duo” and “Great Games on iPhone Duo.” Individual listings can also display the “Made for iPhone Duo” badge , helping customers identify apps adapted for the folding display before downloading them.

Among the recently updated apps are Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, Zoom, Etsy and Halide Mark III. Their support is particularly useful for people who want to work with documents, manage messages or use creative tools on the larger screen without switching to an iPad.

The growing catalog does not mean every iPhone app has been redesigned for Duo, or that every optimized app will make equally good use of its displays. Developers can continue improving layouts and interactions after an initial update, so the experience may differ from one app to another.

Apple opened submissions for iPhone Duo-optimized apps ahead of the phone’s October 23 release, giving developers tools to test different screen sizes, orientations and folding positions. The latest figure suggests that work is continuing beyond launch as more familiar apps gain dedicated support.

sources.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
passages: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.
The cybersecurity giant has a history of buying innovation rather than building it in-house, and it has ramped up dealmaking this year in response to rising AI-driven cyberattacks.
Several of Clutch’s competitors have also been acquired.
Meanwhile, Cisco bought Menlo Ventures-backed Astrix for roughly $400 million , Calcalist reported.
Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source.
The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.

sources.title: Palo Alto Networks Eyes $500M Clutch Buy in AI Security Arms Race
passages: Palo Alto Networks is in advanced talks to acquire Clutch, an AI agent security startup, for roughly $500 million, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Just days ago, CrowdStrike dropped $500M on AI security duo Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in a double acquisition targeting the exact same market.

With CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and now Palo Alto all making aggressive moves in this space within weeks of each other, the message to enterprises is clear: autonomous AI systems require fundamentally new security approaches, and the companies that provide them will command premium valuations.

Venture investors have poured billions into AI security startups over the past year, with companies like Armadin - founded by former FireEye CEO Kevin Mandia - raising $255.5M at a $2.5B valuation to build AI agent swarms for enterprise security.
If completed, the purchase would give the enterprise security giant a critical foothold in protecting the autonomous AI agents now flooding corporate networks.

The company's existing platform already includes some AI-focused security tools, but Clutch would bring specialized capabilities for monitoring AI agent behavior, detecting anomalies, and preventing autonomous systems from accessing sensitive data or taking unauthorized actions.
The rapid exit timeline - Clutch is still a relatively young company - suggests just how urgent the need has become for established security vendors to acquire rather than build these capabilities.
As companies rush to deploy these agents for everything from customer service to code generation, the security implications have become impossible to ignore.
Clutch's technology addresses this next phase, providing the guardrails enterprises need to deploy AI agents without creating massive new attack surfaces.

extraction.body: Palo Alto Networks is in advanced talks to acquire Clutch, an AI agent security startup, for roughly $500 million, according to sources familiar with the matter. The deal would value the young company at nearly six times its last funding round valuation of $85 million and marks the latest mega-acquisition in the exploding AI security market. If completed, the purchase would give the enterprise security giant a critical foothold in protecting the autonomous AI agents now flooding corporate networks. Palo Alto Networks is closing in on a roughly $500 million deal to buy Clutch, a startup focused on securing AI agents, according to multiple sources with knowledge of the negotiations. The talks come as enterprise security vendors scramble to address the security risks posed by autonomous AI systems now being deployed across corporate environments. Clutch was last valued at just $85 million, meaning Palo Alto is willing to pay nearly six times that figure to acquire the technology. The startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and SignalFire, has built a platform specifically designed to monitor and secure AI agents - the autonomous software systems that can take actions, access data, and make decisions without human oversight. As companies rush to deploy these agents for everything from customer service to code generation, the security implications have become impossible to ignore. The deal talks reveal how quickly AI agent security has transformed from a niche concern into a must-have capability for enterprise security platforms. Just days ago, CrowdStrike dropped $500M on AI security duo Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in a double acquisition targeting the exact same market. Palo Alto Networks has been methodically building its AI security portfolio through a combination of internal development and strategic acquisitions. The company's existing platform already includes some AI-focused security tools, but Clutch would bring specialized capabilities for monitoring AI agent behavior, detecting anomalies, and preventing autonomous systems from accessing sensitive data or taking unauthorized actions. The valuation jump reflects both Clutch's technology and the broader market dynamics. Venture investors have poured billions into AI security startups over the past year, with companies like Armadin - founded by former FireEye CEO Kevin Mandia - raising $255.5M at a $2.5B valuation to build AI agent swarms for enterprise security. Even Nvidia has entered the space, launching an open agent safety platform that provides full-stack governance for AI systems. For Palo Alto Networks, the acquisition would address a critical gap in its product lineup at a moment when customers are demanding comprehensive AI security solutions. The company competes directly with CrowdStrike, Fortinet, and other security vendors who are all racing to offer end-to-end protection for AI deployments. Losing ground in this emerging category could mean losing access to the next generation of enterprise security budgets. Lightspeed and SignalFire, Clutch's primary backers, stand to see substantial returns if the deal closes at the reported $500 million figure. Both firms have been active investors in the AI security space, betting early that protecting autonomous systems would become a major enterprise priority. The rapid exit timeline - Clutch is still a relatively young company - suggests just how urgent the need has become for established security vendors to acquire rather than build these capabilities. The deal structure and timeline remain fluid, and there's no guarantee the talks will result in a completed transaction. But the momentum is clear: enterprise security is being rebuilt around AI, and the companies that can't secure autonomous agents risk becoming irrelevant. Palo Alto Networks appears determined not to let that happen, even if it means paying a significant premium for a startup that was valued at a fraction of the purchase price just months ago. Early AI security concerns focused on model vulnerabilities, data poisoning, and prompt injection attacks. But as companies move from chatbots to autonomous agents that can access systems, move data, and take actions on behalf of users, the security model has to evolve. Clutch's technology addresses this next phase, providing the guardrails enterprises need to deploy AI agents without creating massive new attack surfaces. Palo Alto Networks' pursuit of Clutch at a 6x valuation premium signals that AI agent security has moved from emerging concern to existential priority for enterprise security vendors. With CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and now Palo Alto all making aggressive moves in this space within weeks of each other, the message to enterprises is clear: autonomous AI systems require fundamentally new security approaches, and the companies that provide them will command premium valuations. As AI agents proliferate across corporate networks, expect more acquisitions, more funding rounds, and more competition for the startups building the guardrails that make autonomous AI safe for enterprise deployment.

coreStoryFacts.text: Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security , a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.
The cybersecurity giant has a history of buying innovation rather than building it in-house, and it has ramped up dealmaking this year in response to rising AI-driven cyberattacks.
Several of Clutch’s competitors have also been acquired.
Meanwhile, Cisco bought Menlo Ventures-backed Astrix for roughly $400 million , Calcalist reported.
Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source.
The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.

Palo Alto Networks is in advanced talks to acquire Clutch, an AI agent security startup, for roughly $500 million, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Just days ago, CrowdStrike dropped $500M on AI security duo Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in a double acquisition targeting the exact same market.

With CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and now Palo Alto all making aggressive moves in this space within weeks of each other, the message to enterprises is clear: autonomous AI systems require fundamentally new security approaches, and the companies that provide them will command premium valuations.

Venture investors have poured billions into AI security startups over the past year, with companies like Armadin - founded by former FireEye CEO Kevin Mandia - raising $255.5M at a $2.5B valuation to build AI agent swarms for enterprise security.
If completed, the purchase would give the enterprise security giant a critical foothold in protecting the autonomous AI agents now flooding corporate networks.

The company's existing platform already includes some AI-focused security tools, but Clutch would bring specialized capabilities for monitoring AI agent behavior, detecting anomalies, and preventing autonomous systems from accessing sensitive data or taking unauthorized actions.
The rapid exit timeline - Clutch is still a relatively young company - suggests just how urgent the need has become for established security vendors to acquire rather than build these capabilities.
As companies rush to deploy these agents for everything from customer service to code generation, the security implications have become impossible to ignore.

The transaction valued Console at $500 million in stock and cash, TechCrunch reported. Other VC-backed companies that Palo Alto Networks has scooped up this year include NEA-backed Embrace, for $325 million ; Chronosphere, an observability platform backed by Greylock and Lux Capital, for $2.95 billion ; and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $231 million , according to regulatory filings. Several of Clutch’s competitors have also been acquired. Cyera, a cybersecurity startup valued at $12 billion earlier this year, acquired Oasis Security, which, like Clutch, focuses on managing AI agents’ access to systems, for $1 billion . sources.title: Palo Alto Networks Eyes $500M Clutch Buy in AI Security Arms Race
passages: Palo Alto Networks is in advanced talks to acquire Clutch, an AI agent security startup, for roughly $500 million, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Just days ago, CrowdStrike dropped $500M on AI security duo Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in a double acquisition targeting the exact same market.

With CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and now Palo Alto all making aggressive moves in this space within weeks of each other, the message to enterprises is clear: autonomous AI systems require fundamentally new security approaches, and the companies that provide them will command premium valuations.

Venture investors have poured billions into AI security startups over the past year, with companies like Armadin - founded by former FireEye CEO Kevin Mandia - raising $255.5M at a $2.5B valuation to build AI agent swarms for enterprise security.
If completed, the purchase would give the enterprise security giant a critical foothold in protecting the autonomous AI agents now flooding corporate networks.

The company's existing platform already includes some AI-focused security tools, but Clutch would bring specialized capabilities for monitoring AI agent behavior, detecting anomalies, and preventing autonomous systems from accessing sensitive data or taking unauthorized actions.
The rapid exit timeline - Clutch is still a relatively young company - suggests just how urgent the need has become for established security vendors to acquire rather than build these capabilities.
As companies rush to deploy these agents for everything from customer service to code generation, the security implications have become impossible to ignore.
Clutch's technology addresses this next phase, providing the guardrails enterprises need to deploy AI agents without creating massive new attack surfaces.
