The plans would mark a sharp shift from the Republican-led Congress, where lawmakers largely focused on promoting AI development and declined to pass legislation restricting aspects of the technology at a time when voters turned against the rapid development of data centers and their extensive power needs.

Democrats plan on introducing bills aimed at shielding consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centers, requiring independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarifying when AI companies can be held liable for harm caused by their products, they said.
Any legislation would face steep odds while President Donald Trump remains in the White House, as he has repeatedly dismissed calls to write mandatory rules for AI technology.

But Democratic lawmakers and outside advocates said control of congressional committees would give the party a platform to advance proposals, compel testimony from industry leaders and build support for action if AI systems cause real-world harm. Representative Greg Casar, a Texas Democrat and chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, already said this week that AI executives should be called to testify under oath.

Federal government restrictions on AI development could hurt the industry’s profits if they slow the release of new models or prompt the companies to change how their AI tools perform to address concerns that their products are harming people.

Technology shares sold off dramatically on Thursday on growing concerns that a new Congress will slow AI development, but also on fears that the massive capital expense on building out AI will not yield sufficient returns.

Senator Chuck Schumer, a New York Democrat who is expected to become majority leader, said on Thursday at an event in Washington that protecting consumers from higher energy costs linked to the rapid expansion of data centers would be among his priorities next year.

Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts, one of the Democratic Party’s leading voices on AI policy, plans to push legislation requiring independent experts to evaluate leading AI models against safety standards, said Francis Grubar, her deputy chief of staff. Trahan will also pursue legislation clarifying that companies can be held responsible when AI systems act in harmful ways, he said.

Representative Zoe Lofgren, a Democrat from California who is seeking to chair the House Science Committee, said Democrats would focus on developing “responsible regulations for AI while also fostering innovation.”

Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan Democrat who won a Senate seat on Tuesday, called during his campaign for an independent agency to oversee AI regulation with the power to police tech companies developing the technology.

Public concern about AI is already high. Most US voters think Trump’s administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to ​write new regulations for the technology, according to a Reuters poll published in October. A crisis could build enough support to overcome presidential opposition to AI regulation, said Ed Mills, who manages policy research at Raymond James.
“The probability of legislation is much higher than people anticipate,” he said.

Congress can override a presidential veto with the backing of two-thirds of lawmakers in both chambers. Democrats could also try to insert AI regulation into routine bills that must pass Congress each year, Mills said.

Democrats also plan to use their new authority to intensify scrutiny of the industry’s most powerful companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic. Lofgren and other Democratic House committee leaders in October asked OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Alphabet’s Google and SpaceX to detail their security practices and report instances of their AI tools taking actions that their designers did not intend.

extraction.body: Following the recent severe escalation in the conflict in Sudan, Commissioner Hadja Lahbib joined 32 countries to reiterate EU's full support to the people of Sudan and reaffirm its commitment to the respect of international humanitarian law: 'We express grave concern over the continued deadly unlawful attacks on civilians, civilian infrastructure and humanitarian operations as heavy fighting across the Kordofan and Darfur States continues. The recent severe escalation in drone and aerial attacks including those affecting displaced civilians, health facilities, food convoys and areas near humanitarian compounds have resulted in a significant number of civilian deaths and injuries and is further disrupting humanitarian access and supply lines. In recent weeks alone, drone and rocket strikes on trucks and warehouses of the World Food Programme, as well as on health facilities, have resulted in the deaths and severe injuries of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and the destruction of urgently needed humanitarian supplies and infrastructure. Intentional attacks against humanitarian personnel, vehicles, or supplies, as well as wilfully impeding relief supplies, are contrary to international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. The Darfur and Kordofan States remain at the epicenter of the world's largest humanitarian and protection crisis. Sexual and gender-based violence is rampant, famine is confirmed and severe hunger continues to spread. Up to 100,000 people have been displaced in recent months in the Kordofan states alone. According to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, violations and abuses committed by the RSF and its allied militias in and around El Fasher last October risk being repeated in the Kordofan region. We urgently repeat our call to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and their allied militias to immediately cease hostilities. We condemn the abhorrent violence against civilians, particularly women and children and all serious violations of international humanitarian law in the strongest terms. These violations may amount to war crimes or crimes against humanity and must be promptly and impartially investigated, with those responsible for international crimes brought to justice. All parties must respect international humanitarian law which includes an obligation to allow and facilitate the rapid, safe and unimpeded access of food, medicine, and other essential supplies to civilians in need. Civilians including humanitarian personnel must be protected at all times, particularly women and girls, who remain at risk of sexual and gender-based violence. Those fleeing must be granted safe passage. We stand with the people of Sudan and humanitarian organisations – local and international – who are working tirelessly and under extremely challenging conditions to assist them.' extraction.body: The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, welcomed Beate Meinl-Reisinger, Federal Minister for European and International Affairs of the Republic of Austria, to Ottawa on November 6, 2026. November 6, 2026 – Ottawa, Ontario - Global Affairs Canada The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, welcomed Beate Meinl-Reisinger, Federal Minister for European and International Affairs of the Republic of Austria, to Ottawa on November 6, 2026. In a period of increasing geopolitical uncertainty, the Ministers reaffirmed the close and growing partnership between Canada and Austria and underscored the importance of cooperation among like-minded partners to support international peace and security, strengthen economic resilience, and uphold international law. The Ministers welcomed the high-level political dialogue held in Ottawa last month and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on foreign policy, multilateral cooperation, economic and trade exchange. The Ministers also welcomed the inaugural Canada-Austria Political-Military Dialogue, held at the senior official level in Vienna this week, and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on security and defence issues. As Canada and Austria prepare to mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027, the Ministers welcomed the strong people-to-people ties, which continue to enrich the relationship between the two countries. The Ministers welcomed the strong foundation of bilateral trade and investment and expressed their determination to deepen cooperation in areas of growing strategic importance. They committed to advancing collaboration in critical minerals, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, science, technology and innovation, recognizing the complementary strengths of Canadian and Austrian industries and research institutions. They also looked forward to the launch of exploratory discussions in Vienna next week on a bilateral MoU on Science, Technology and Innovation (STI). They welcomed ongoing discussions between Canadian and Austrian companies and institutions and encouraged officials to identify opportunities to strengthen resilient transatlantic supply chains. The Ministers welcomed efforts underway toward enhanced bilateral cooperation in research and innovation and tasked officials to continue exploring mechanisms to support greater collaboration between Canadian and Austrian researchers, innovators, and technology firms in particular with regard to sustainability. Minister Meinl-Reisinger welcomed the outcomes of the recent Canada-EU Leaders' Summit and reaffirmed Austria's support for a deeper and more ambitious Canada-EU partnership, creating an ever closer association between the EU and Canada. The Ministers highlighted the importance of strengthening cooperation between Canada and the European Union on economic security, defence industrial cooperation, innovation, clean technology, critical minerals, emerging technologies, and democratic resilience. They reaffirmed their support for the full implementation of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and acknowledged its contribution to expanding trade and investment opportunities on both sides of the Atlantic over the past 10 years. Minister Anand congratulated Austria on its election to the United Nations Security Council for the 2027-2028 term. The Ministers reaffirmed their shared commitment to effective multilateralism and agreed to deepen Canada-Austria cooperation during Austria's Security Council tenure. They instructed officials to identify practical opportunities for collaboration on shared priorities, including the protection of civilians in armed conflict, Women, Peace and Security, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of international humanitarian and human rights law. The Ministers also expressed interest in exploring opportunities for joint initiatives and events at the United Nations in New York during Austria's Security Council term. The Ministers reaffirmed their unwavering support for Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. They condemned Russia's recent attacks affecting civilian infrastructure and humanitarian facilities in Ukraine and the broader pattern of illegal and unjustifiable conduct associated with Russia's aggression, and reiterated their commitment to a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace consistent with the UN Charter and international law. The Ministers agreed to strengthen Canada-Austria cooperation in support of Ukraine, particularly on recovery and reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, energy security and resilience, the return of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred and unlawfully deported by Russia, the release of unlawfully detained civilians and prisoners of war, and assistance for veterans and their families. They underscored the importance of accountability for war crimes and violations of international law. The Ministers reaffirmed their shared interest in a stable, secure, democratic, and prosperous Western Balkans. They emphasized the importance of advancing reforms, strengthening democratic institutions, combating corruption, supporting good neighbourly relations and regional reconciliation. The Ministers underlined that a pathway toward European integration remains essential for long-term regional stability and prosperity. They agreed to continue coordinating closely on developments across the Western Balkans. Recognizing the growing importance of the bilateral relationship, the Ministers agreed to maintain regular political dialogue and close coordination to advance shared priorities, including economic security, sustainability, innovation, support for Ukraine, multilateral cooperation, human rights, and international peace and security, including through the Women Foreign Ministers’ Network. The Ministers also welcomed the inaugural Canada-Austria Political-Military Dialogue, held at the senior official level in Vienna this week, and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on security and defence issues.

As Canada and Austria prepare to mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027, the Ministers welcomed the strong people-to-people ties, which continue to enrich the relationship between the two countries.
The Ministers welcomed the strong foundation of bilateral trade and investment and expressed their determination to deepen cooperation in areas of growing strategic importance.

They committed to advancing collaboration in critical minerals, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, science, technology and innovation, recognizing the complementary strengths of Canadian and Austrian industries and research institutions. They also looked forward to the launch of exploratory discussions in Vienna next week on a bilateral MoU on Science, Technology and Innovation (STI).
They welcomed ongoing discussions between Canadian and Austrian companies and institutions and encouraged officials to identify opportunities to strengthen resilient transatlantic supply chains.

The Ministers welcomed efforts underway toward enhanced bilateral cooperation in research and innovation and tasked officials to continue exploring mechanisms to support greater collaboration between Canadian and Austrian researchers, innovators, and technology firms in particular with regard to sustainability.

Minister Meinl-Reisinger welcomed the outcomes of the recent Canada-EU Leaders' Summit and reaffirmed Austria's support for a deeper and more ambitious Canada-EU partnership, creating an ever closer association between the EU and Canada.

The Ministers highlighted the importance of strengthening cooperation between Canada and the European Union on economic security, defence industrial cooperation, innovation, clean technology, critical minerals, emerging technologies, and democratic resilience.

They reaffirmed their support for the full implementation of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and acknowledged its contribution to expanding trade and investment opportunities on both sides of the Atlantic over the past 10 years.
Minister Anand congratulated Austria on its election to the United Nations Security Council for the 2027-2028 term.

The Ministers reaffirmed their shared commitment to effective multilateralism and agreed to deepen Canada-Austria cooperation during Austria's Security Council tenure. They instructed officials to identify practical opportunities for collaboration on shared priorities, including the protection of civilians in armed conflict, Women, Peace and Security, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of international humanitarian and human rights law.
The Ministers also expressed interest in exploring opportunities for joint initiatives and events at the United Nations in New York during Austria's Security Council term.
The Ministers reaffirmed their unwavering support for Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

They condemned Russia's recent attacks affecting civilian infrastructure and humanitarian facilities in Ukraine and the broader pattern of illegal and unjustifiable conduct associated with Russia's aggression, and reiterated their commitment to a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace consistent with the UN Charter and international law.

The Ministers agreed to strengthen Canada-Austria cooperation in support of Ukraine, particularly on recovery and reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, energy security and resilience, the return of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred and unlawfully deported by Russia, the release of unlawfully detained civilians and prisoners of war, and assistance for veterans and their families. They underscored the importance of accountability for war crimes and violations of international law.
The Ministers reaffirmed their shared interest in a stable, secure, democratic, and prosperous Western Balkans.

They emphasized the importance of advancing reforms, strengthening democratic institutions, combating corruption, supporting good neighbourly relations and regional reconciliation. The Ministers underlined that a pathway toward European integration remains essential for long-term regional stability and prosperity.
They agreed to continue coordinating closely on developments across the Western Balkans.

Recognizing the growing importance of the bilateral relationship, the Ministers agreed to maintain regular political dialogue and close coordination to advance shared priorities, including economic security, sustainability, innovation, support for Ukraine, multilateral cooperation, human rights, and international peace and security, including through the Women Foreign Ministers’ Network.

extraction.body: Following the recent severe escalation in the conflict in Sudan, Commissioner Hadja Lahbib joined 32 countries to reiterate EU's full support to the people of Sudan and reaffirm its commitment to the respect of international humanitarian law: 'We express grave concern over the continued deadly unlawful attacks on civilians, civilian infrastructure and humanitarian operations as heavy fighting across the Kordofan and Darfur States continues. The recent severe escalation in drone and aerial attacks including those affecting displaced civilians, health facilities, food convoys and areas near humanitarian compounds have resulted in a significant number of civilian deaths and injuries and is further disrupting humanitarian access and supply lines. In recent weeks alone, drone and rocket strikes on trucks and warehouses of the World Food Programme, as well as on health facilities, have resulted in the deaths and severe injuries of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and the destruction of urgently needed humanitarian supplies and infrastructure. Intentional attacks against humanitarian personnel, vehicles, or supplies, as well as wilfully impeding relief supplies, are contrary to international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. The Darfur and Kordofan States remain at the epicenter of the world's largest humanitarian and protection crisis. Sexual and gender-based violence is rampant, famine is confirmed and severe hunger continues to spread. Up to 100,000 people have been displaced in recent months in the Kordofan states alone. According to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, violations and abuses committed by the RSF and its allied militias in and around El Fasher last October risk being repeated in the Kordofan region. We urgently repeat our call to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and their allied militias to immediately cease hostilities. We condemn the abhorrent violence against civilians, particularly women and children and all serious violations of international humanitarian law in the strongest terms. These violations may amount to war crimes or crimes against humanity and must be promptly and impartially investigated, with those responsible for international crimes brought to justice. All parties must respect international humanitarian law which includes an obligation to allow and facilitate the rapid, safe and unimpeded access of food, medicine, and other essential supplies to civilians in need. Civilians including humanitarian personnel must be protected at all times, particularly women and girls, who remain at risk of sexual and gender-based violence. Those fleeing must be granted safe passage. We stand with the people of Sudan and humanitarian organisations – local and international – who are working tirelessly and under extremely challenging conditions to assist them.' passages: The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, welcomed Beate Meinl-Reisinger, Federal Minister for European and International Affairs of the Republic of Austria, to Ottawa on November 6, 2026.

In a period of increasing geopolitical uncertainty, the Ministers reaffirmed the close and growing partnership between Canada and Austria and underscored the importance of cooperation among like-minded partners to support international peace and security, strengthen economic resilience, and uphold international law.

They instructed officials to identify practical opportunities for collaboration on shared priorities, including the protection of civilians in armed conflict, Women, Peace and Security, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of international humanitarian and human rights law.
Minister Anand congratulated Austria on its election to the United Nations Security Council for the 2027-2028 term.

The Ministers agreed to strengthen Canada-Austria cooperation in support of Ukraine, particularly on recovery and reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, energy security and resilience, the return of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred and unlawfully deported by Russia, the release of unlawfully detained civilians and prisoners of war, and assistance for veterans and their families.
The Ministers underlined that a pathway toward European integration remains essential for long-term regional stability and prosperity.

The Ministers welcomed the high-level political dialogue held in Ottawa last month and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on foreign policy, multilateral cooperation, economic and trade exchange.

November 6, 2026 – Ottawa, Ontario - Global Affairs Canada The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, welcomed Beate Meinl-Reisinger, Federal Minister for European and International Affairs of the Republic of Austria, to Ottawa on November 6, 2026. In a period of increasing geopolitical uncertainty, the Ministers reaffirmed the close and growing partnership between Canada and Austria and underscored the importance of cooperation among like-minded partners to support international peace and security, strengthen economic resilience, and uphold international law. The Ministers welcomed the high-level political dialogue held in Ottawa last month and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on foreign policy, multilateral cooperation, economic and trade exchange. The Ministers also welcomed the inaugural Canada-Austria Political-Military Dialogue, held at the senior official level in Vienna this week, and noted its contribution to strengthening bilateral cooperation on security and defence issues. As Canada and Austria prepare to mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027, the Ministers welcomed the strong people-to-people ties, which continue to enrich the relationship between the two countries. The Ministers welcomed the strong foundation of bilateral trade and investment and expressed their determination to deepen cooperation in areas of growing strategic importance. They committed to advancing collaboration in critical minerals, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, science, technology and innovation, recognizing the complementary strengths of Canadian and Austrian industries and research institutions. They also looked forward to the launch of exploratory discussions in Vienna next week on a bilateral MoU on Science, Technology and Innovation (STI). They welcomed ongoing discussions between Canadian and Austrian companies and institutions and encouraged officials to identify opportunities to strengthen resilient transatlantic supply chains. The Ministers welcomed efforts underway toward enhanced bilateral cooperation in research and innovation and tasked officials to continue exploring mechanisms to support greater collaboration between Canadian and Austrian researchers, innovators, and technology firms in particular with regard to sustainability. Minister Meinl-Reisinger welcomed the outcomes of the recent Canada-EU Leaders' Summit and reaffirmed Austria's support for a deeper and more ambitious Canada-EU partnership, creating an ever closer association between the EU and Canada. The Ministers highlighted the importance of strengthening cooperation between Canada and the European Union on economic security, defence industrial cooperation, innovation, clean technology, critical minerals, emerging technologies, and democratic resilience. They reaffirmed their support for the full implementation of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and acknowledged its contribution to expanding trade and investment opportunities on both sides of the Atlantic over the past 10 years. Minister Anand congratulated Austria on its election to the United Nations Security Council for the 2027-2028 term. The Ministers reaffirmed their shared commitment to effective multilateralism and agreed to deepen Canada-Austria cooperation during Austria's Security Council tenure. They instructed officials to identify practical opportunities for collaboration on shared priorities, including the protection of civilians in armed conflict, Women, Peace and Security, conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of international humanitarian and human rights law. The Ministers also expressed interest in exploring opportunities for joint initiatives and events at the United Nations in New York during Austria's Security Council term. The Ministers reaffirmed their unwavering support for Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. They condemned Russia's recent attacks affecting civilian infrastructure and humanitarian facilities in Ukraine and the broader pattern of illegal and unjustifiable conduct associated with Russia's aggression, and reiterated their commitment to a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace consistent with the UN Charter and international law. The Ministers agreed to strengthen Canada-Austria cooperation in support of Ukraine, particularly on recovery and reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, energy security and resilience, the return of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred and unlawfully deported by Russia, the release of unlawfully detained civilians and prisoners of war, and assistance for veterans and their families. They underscored the importance of accountability for war crimes and violations of international law. The Ministers reaffirmed their shared interest in a stable, secure, democratic, and prosperous Western Balkans. They emphasized the importance of advancing reforms, strengthening democratic institutions, combating corruption, supporting good neighbourly relations and regional reconciliation. The Ministers underlined that a pathway toward European integration remains essential for long-term regional stability and prosperity. They agreed to continue coordinating closely on developments across the Western Balkans. Recognizing the growing importance of the bilateral relationship, the Ministers agreed to maintain regular political dialogue and close coordination to advance shared priorities, including economic security, sustainability, innovation, support for Ukraine, multilateral cooperation, human rights, and international peace and security, including through the Women Foreign Ministers’ Network. sources.title: TSMC considers making advanced memory chips, The Information reports
passages: Nov 6 (Reuters) - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co is considering expanding into advanced memory chip production, in a move that would allow it to capture a larger share of the AI hardware market, The Information reported on Friday.

TSMC and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. o TSMC could opt to build new factories for advanced memory chips, but it was not clear when it plans to begin production, according to the report o The world's largest chip manufacturer is also exploring acquiring an existing plant and converting it for memory production, the report said, similar to Micron's move this year to buy a fab and convert it for DRAM output o DRAM, or dynamic random access memory, chips are used to store data temporarily in devices.

sources.title: After the midterms, is the AI industry in for a rough two years? - Yahoo Finance

extraction.body: Democrats' historic victories in this week's U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry. The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more restrictions on data center development. And even when data centers weren't on the ballot directly, they were a major talking point, with newly-elected Democratic governors and congressmembers likely to support additional regulation . On the latest episode of TechCrunch's Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O'Kane, and Anthony Ha discuss what the election will mean for the tech industry moving forward — not just when it comes to data centers (which OpenAI is already trying to rebrand ), but also increased government scrutiny of Big Tech.

passages: Patrick Yaroch, a former FBI agent accused of stealing approximately $1 million in cryptocurrency, is scheduled to plead guilty on Thursday, according to court records.

He allegedly accessed classified records for cases that weren't assigned to him and gained access to digital cryptocurrency wallets belonging to an adversarial nation, which court records do not name, the Washington Post reported .

extraction.body: Patrick Yaroch, 37, had planned to "build a life in Portugal" after he "misused his access to classified information to enrich himself," federal prosecutors in Virginia said in legal filings. Patrick Yaroch, a former FBI agent accused of stealing approximately $1 million in cryptocurrency, is scheduled to plead guilty on Thursday, according to court records. Yaroch, 37, was a supervisor in the FBI's counterintelligence and espionage division until his arrest this summer. He allegedly accessed classified records for cases that weren't assigned to him and gained access to digital cryptocurrency wallets belonging to an adversarial nation, which court records do not name, the Washington Post reported . He had planned to "build a life in Portugal" after he "misused his access to classified information to enrich himself," federal prosecutors in Virginia said in legal filings. Yaroch is scheduled to appear before a federal judge in Alexandria, Virginia, for a plea agreement hearing on Thursday, according to an entry on the court’s calendar. The judge must approve any plea deal before it's finalized.

He allegedly accessed classified records for cases that weren't assigned to him and gained access to digital cryptocurrency wallets belonging to an adversarial nation, which court records do not name, the Washington Post reported . The judge must approve any plea deal before it's finalized.

Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. All of the stolen SOL, about $87 million at Elliptic’s prices, has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of it ending as bitcoin. Most early Tron laundering — about $220 million in TRX — has also run, a flow Bitcoin Magazine noted when covering the quiet shutdown of the T3 Financial Crime Unit before the hack. Only small parts of the main ether and NEAR piles have moved. Some converted bitcoin has gone into Wasabi-style coinjoins — about 33 BTC, or $2.5 million, since Nov. 1 — and about $1.1 million in ether and SOL entered the Privacy Cash pool before that service paused deposits. Elliptic said the speed points to conventional automation, not an AI agent making live decisions: fixed timing, set amounts, blind retries and new tactics introduced hours apart. U.S. bank supervisors have already checked in with lenders after the Binance breach. For bitcoin markets, the nearer question is how much more of the remaining ~192 million XRP — and eventually the parked ether — gets turned into BTC before anyone tries to cash out. The test now is whether THORChain operators and other bridges keep blocking the published attacker addresses fast enough to slow the XRP-to-bitcoin pipe, or whether the rest of that pile follows the same overnight path the first $50 million already took. sources.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple - TechCrunch
passages: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch.
But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front.

The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year.
On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve .
The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added.
Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo.
However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon.

extraction.body: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu. Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve . “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note. Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon. extraction.body: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu. Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve . “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note. Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon. sources.title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
passages: Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027.

Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would.
Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added.
He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip.
Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month.
“Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment.
But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational.
Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience.
In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips.
They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that.
So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said.
The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates.
It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens.
Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences.

extraction.body: Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday , Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot. In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month. Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything. “Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said. Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would. “What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.” The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs. In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself. “Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote. Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year. While the company previously said to expect its AI agent sometime in the next year, it’s now more specifically committing to roll out the new technology to consumers in the first half of 2027. The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates. It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens. “Airbnb is back in growth mode,” Chesky told analysts on the Q3 earnings call on Thursday. “It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added. extraction.body: Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday , Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot. In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month. Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything. “Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said. Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would. “What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.” The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs. In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself. “Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote. Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year. extraction.body: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%. Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla. However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse. In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%. In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices. The market fluctuations also come after the sweeping Democrat victory in the midterm elections. A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race. US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring". However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off. Russ Shaw, founder of global tech advocacy firm Tech London Advocates, said the election result was sending a message that a rethink was needed on AI. "The incoming Congress is going to really focus on AI in a very dramatic way," he told the BBC's Business Today. "I'm a big fan of AI, but I'm watching what these companies are doing, and they're not communicating effectively at all, particularly in the US, about what the benefits of AI are all about." Pierre Baqué, chief executive of AI platform Neural Concept, said the share movements were a "necessary market correction" that reflected a legitimate concern about the amount of money being poured into AI infrastructure. "The industry must move beyond unchecked infrastructure investment and demonstrate greater financial discipline," he said. "We are entering a critical transition phase, a market purgatory where raw tech must prove its widespread economic value." Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said it had been a brutal week for markets, and the key question was whether the jump in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq would be sustained. "Once investors have had the weekend to catch their breath, next week could give a clearer indication of whether the tech trade is going down the pan or fighting back." As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures. And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected. Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September . The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important. "The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said. Changes in the FTSE 100 and other indexes are not just for financial experts, they can affect our lives. Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months. Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI own search summaries were affecting ad revenue. extraction.body: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%. Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla. However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse. In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%. In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices. The market fluctuations also come after the sweeping Democrat victory in the midterm elections. A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race. US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring". However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off. Russ Shaw, founder of global tech advocacy firm Tech London Advocates, said the election result was sending a message that a rethink was needed on AI. "The incoming Congress is going to really focus on AI in a very dramatic way," he told the BBC's Business Today. "I'm a big fan of AI, but I'm watching what these companies are doing, and they're not communicating effectively at all, particularly in the US, about what the benefits of AI are all about." Pierre Baqué, chief executive of AI platform Neural Concept, said the share movements were a "necessary market correction" that reflected a legitimate concern about the amount of money being poured into AI infrastructure. "The industry must move beyond unchecked infrastructure investment and demonstrate greater financial discipline," he said. "We are entering a critical transition phase, a market purgatory where raw tech must prove its widespread economic value." Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said it had been a brutal week for markets, and the key question was whether the jump in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq would be sustained. "Once investors have had the weekend to catch their breath, next week could give a clearer indication of whether the tech trade is going down the pan or fighting back." As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures. And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected. Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September . The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important. "The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said. Changes in the FTSE 100 and other indexes are not just for financial experts, they can affect our lives. Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months. Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI own search summaries were affecting ad revenue.
